children: SLB reported higher revenue in the recent quarter as business in the Middle East began to gradually recover, following a challenging start to the year.

The oilfield-services company, formerly known as Schlumberger, on Friday posted third-quarter profit of $735 million, or 49 cents a share, compared with $739 million, or 50 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out certain one-time items, earnings came in at 64 cents a share. Analysts surveyed by FactSet expected adjusted earnings of 62 cents a share.
Revenue climbed 5.8% to $9.45 billion, topping Wall Street models for $9.27 billion.
North America revenue jumped 24% to $2.4 billion, while international revenue ticked up 1% to $6.99 billion.

Chief Executive Olivier Le Peuch said SLB benefited from growth in North America land, as well as a gradual recovery in the Middle East and broadening international activity in deepwater offshore basins.
"In the Middle East, our business grew 13% sequentially despite late-quarter disruptions," he said.

At the same time, SLB said its data-center-solutions business continues to accelerate, with revenue up 23% sequentially, driven by growing demand, a broader scope of services and geographic expansion in Asia.

"AI is driving unprecedented investment in data center infrastructure, and customers are looking for partners who can deploy quickly, reliably and at scale," Le Peuch said. "Our modular approach is meeting this need today."
Looking ahead, SLB expects "supportive market fundamentals" to remain intact.
"We see a very compelling outlook for 2027, with further upside as Middle East activity recovers," Le Peuch concluded.
